newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan financials surge on warrants issue plan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan financials surge on warrants issue plan.

text.p: Shares in Taiwan's financial sector surged late on Wednesday on news that regulators planned to allow local and foreign institutions to begin issuing warrants on Taiwan blue-chip shares.
With 60 minutes of trading left, financials had surged 4.49 percent while the overall index was up 2.01 percent.
The Big Three state commercial banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan -- all rose by the daily seven percent limit to T$166, T$175 and T$136, respectively.
Buying on financials by state-linked funds also helped to boost the sector, brokers said.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange announced earlier in the day that it planned to allow local and foreign banks or brokerages issue warrants on local blue chips with a market value of more than T$30 billion.
More than 20 listed firms would be eligible, including big financial shares such as the country's big three banks, but the scheme still requires regulatory approval.

"Sentiment was boosted by the warrants news, although it's still a just proposal and even though the eligible firms' share prices will not necessarily rise once warrants start to be issued," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.
